build.summary:
I built pacing-in-lab-scenarios-and-tips. All 5 acceptance criteria are met and the typecheck is clean, but one assertion in another package's test file now fails, and that file isn't on my list to edit. In src/ui/lab/bedsideTips.test.ts, line 85 still expects `raises.procedures` to equal ["pericardiocentesis"] only. It now also contains "pacing" and "tcp", because the pacing tab declares what it raises in the same export; that file's own header said the pacing package would do this. The fix is in outOfScope.

What was built:
- **Three in-lab scenarios** in src/simulation/pacing.ts:
  - inlab-rca-chb-rbbb: block after an RCA injection in known RBBB, slow broad escape, low pressure.
  - inlab-adenosine-avb: adenosine block with no escape rhythm.
  - inlab-amiodarone-avb: block during an amiodarone infusion.
  - Each opens with a choice of waiting (30 s), atropine, a cough, stopping the infusion (amiodarone only), external pacing or a femoral wire, then runs the existing insertion and box stages.
  - The course is pure engine code: applyInitialAction, inLabTick, effectiveScenario (atropine speeds the atrial rate) and rhythmSupported.
- **Exam versions:** each in-lab scenario has a held-out "exam" variant with a different patient. The adenosine scenario also has a "persistent" / "transient" practice pair. getPacingScenario(id, variant) merges the variant in.
- **Pass criteria** (inLabCriteria / inLabPassed): rhythm supported within the scenario's time limit; no coronary sinus position accepted; output at least 3 times the measured threshold (Oxford ch 9, from the lesson text); box left in demand mode; no asynchronous pacing while the patient has a rhythm of their own.
- **Scoring:** scorePacing handles the in-lab runs. The ward scenarios score exactly as before (both versions add up to 100). Scenarios can override the access verdict: femoral is preferred in the lab.
- **Volts or milliamps:** the box output can read either. The engine still works in mA and converts through LEAD_IMPEDANCE_OHM (model parameter). The in-lab scenarios open on a box reading volts, as Oxford's does.
- **Sheath fit:** a sheath the same size as the wire damps rotation (TIGHT_SHEATH_TORQUE).
- **Tips** (src/ui/lab/bedsideTips.ts): pacingTipContext reports phase by stage (assess, access, position, test, troubleshoot), procedures pacing plus tcp while external pacing is on, and bradycardia, hypotension and av-block from the shared patient-events adapter. It also reports the old "pacing" phase, because the bed-pace-* tips still trigger on it until tip-retarget-catchup moves them.
  - Meanwhile refinePacingTips applies their recorded new triggers (from waiting.ts) at display time, so each tip shows at its own stage and the overdrive VT tip stays out of bradycardia runs.
  - pacingTips returns nothing in exams.
  - `raises` is now the union of the two tabs; PERIC_RAISES and PACING_RAISES are exported separately.
- **Launch file:** pacing.launch.ts lists all 7 scenarios under hb-additional-procedures-pacing (the four ward scenarios also under the Academy pacing lessons). Each in-lab scenario is the practice twin of its held-out exam variant. There is one practice link for the transient adenosine variant.
- **PacingLab.tsx:**
  - Opens links itself through useLabLaunch("pacing"); a held-out variant always runs in exam mode.
  - Runs through useLabRun with one logbook row; this replaces recordSim.
  - Shows the mode bar, the tips panel, the initial-management panel with the time since onset, the sheath choice, the V/mA switch, and a pass-criteria panel in the debrief.
  - Outside guided practice the screens show only what an operator would see: no tip location, rhythm label, checklist ticks, route verdicts, "Show me the fix" or verdicts in the log.
  - In DEV builds window.__lab.pacing exposes the context, tips and state, and can step the rhythm.

build.notes:
- **Snapshots:** datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/pacing-in-lab-scenarios-and-tips/ holds the 4 listed files that existed before (pacing.ts, pacing.test.ts, PacingLab.tsx, bedsideTips.ts) plus .started. pacing.launch.ts is new. No browser was used.

- **Sources:** the in-lab clinical content (atropine 1 mg may improve AV conduction, a cough after adenosine, stopping amiodarone, external pacing as the bridge, the femoral route, a sheath larger than the wire, at least 3 times the threshold, demand mode) is taken from lesson hb-additional-procedures-pacing and cites Oxford ch 9/10 and Brilakis 3.7/12.2 in the text. Every rhythm and timing number is a model value.

- **Two output margins:** the in-lab scenarios require 3 times the measured threshold (Oxford, from the lesson). The ward scenarios keep 2 to 3 times (SIM_FACTS 17, which marks a "3 x threshold" rule as unverified from other sources). Both are shown in the UI with their source.

- **1000 ohm impedance:** at this value volts and milliamps read the same number. I chose it so the sourced 1 mA and 1 V anchors agree; the conversion code handles any impedance and the tests also run at 500 ohm. If the owner wants the unit switch to change the numbers on screen, lowering the impedance does it but makes the 1 mA and 1 V acceptability anchors disagree.

- **Tip hook:** the plan named a signature `pacingTipContext(stage, lead, box, faults, flags)`. The built one is `(stage, flags, vitals, prev)`, matching pericardioTipContext, because the context only needs the stage, external pacing on or off, and the monitor's patient events. The lab picks tips with useTipsModule + tipsVisible + pacingTips rather than useContextTips, so it can show each bed-pace tip at its stage while the retargets wait. The visibility rule is the same one.

- **Reachability side effect:** because the context reports the old 'pacing' phase, bed-pace-overdrive-vt now counts as satisfiable in the reachability report. The pacing lab hides it (refinePacingTips) until pacing-overdrive-and-tcp raises 'vt' with procedure 'overdrive'.

- **Behaviour changes that also affect the ward scenarios:**
  - A sheath fit (one size larger / same size) must now be chosen before "Sheath in".
  - The scenario picker is a select box.
  - Supervised, independent and exam runs hide the teaching aids (tip location, rhythm label, checklist ticks, route verdicts, Show me the fix, verdicts in the log).
  - A run writes its logbook row through useLabRun.finish (source 'pacing', so it still maps to the same EPAs) instead of recordSim.
  - Guided practice looks as it did, apart from the units switch and the sheath choice.

- **Small points:**
  - Atropine here is a scenario action that changes the model's atrial rate. The pacing lab has no PatientEngine, so giveDrug and pharmacology.ts are not involved.
  - The in-lab 'femoral wire' action is recorded when the femoral route is chosen; a learner can still switch to the jugular route in the access stage.

review.verdict:
Pass with fixes. The package needs two fixes to its own files, and two edits to files it doesn't own, before it closes. The design is fully built. The 4 package test files pass (60/60) and `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` is clean, both run by me.

What checks out:
- The engine diffs match the plan: three in-lab scenarios with the initial-management course, held-out exam variants plus the persistent and transient adenosine pair, all 5 pass criteria, volts or milliamps through a labelled lead impedance, and the sheath fit.
- Ward scoring still adds up to 100, so dividing by the maximum changes nothing there.
- The tip context and raises are wired, refinePacingTips hides the overdrive tip, and practiceIndex lists every scenario and the transient link but no held-out variant.
- Every clinical statement I checked against src/content/manual/cath-handbook/06-additional-procedures.ts is in the lesson text. That covers atropine 1 mg, the cough, adenosine doses above 100 mcg in the RCA, the 3 V start, a threshold of 1 V or less, at least three times the threshold, a sheath larger than the wire, the femoral route, amiodarone (Brilakis 3.7), and isoprenaline seldom improving conduction.
- The other files under src/ that are newer than .started are bench, closure and access files from other packages; none touch pacing.

Remaining problems:
- One test in another package's file now fails: bedsideTips.test.ts:85.
- One ground-truth leak remains on the live exam screen, in the test checklist.
- In-lab actions disappear once the femoral wire is chosen.
- Pressing External pacing earns credit without any pacing.
- There is no docs/realism/facts entry for the model parameters.
- One header comment is stale.
- Some acceptance tests are weaker than they look.

findings.where: src/ui/bedside/PacingLab.tsx TestChecklist, around lines 1455-1470 (`scenarioDependent ? ... : ...` and the `sensOk` row)
findings.problem: This leaks ground truth onto live screens outside guided practice. `scenarioDependent={!sensingTestable(sc, faults)}` reads model truth (sc.dependent and the intrinsic rate) and, in exam, supervised and independent runs, shows the row 'Pacing dependent: do not turn the rate down to test sensing' with an Acknowledge button. That gives away the scored sensing decision: sensingSkippedDependent earns points in scorePacing. In inlab-adenosine-avb and its exam variant it also announces that there is no escape rhythm. The sensOk row also shows the computed advice `(${recommendedSensitivity(sensingMeasured)} mV or lower)` in every mode, although the builder hid the same 'half =' hint in the box panel outside guided practice.
findings.fix: Use the dependent or testable split only when `guided`. Outside guided practice, render one neutral sensing row: 'Sensing: if the patient has an intrinsic rhythm above the lowest box rate, turn the rate below it and find where the SENSE light stops; if the patient is pacing dependent, do not turn the rate down.' Show the Acknowledge ('Pacing dependent: sensing not tested') button whenever `!sensingSkipped && sensingMeasured === null`, so the learner makes the call. Wrap the recommendedSensitivity text in `guided && ...`. In PacingLab.test.ts, assert that the exam render of inlab-adenosine-avb~exam does not contain 'Pacing dependent'.

findings.where: src/ui/bedside/PacingLab.tsx: initialAction 'femoral-wire' (setStage("access")) and the `stage === "assess"` block that alone renders InLabChoices
findings.problem: InLabChoices renders only in the assess stage. Pressing 'Femoral venous wire', or 'Prepare' through the access flow, moves to the access stage. From then on atropine, the cough and 'Stop the amiodarone infusion' can no longer be chosen for the rest of the run. In inlab-amiodarone-avb, `expected` is ["stop-infusion", "femoral-wire"]. A learner who starts the wire first, which is reasonable, can never stop the infusion and loses 10 of the 20 initial-management points. Clinically, stopping an infusion or giving atropine while the wire goes in is normal. The 'Conducted rhythm back: finish the case' button also exists only in assess, so a transient block that recovers during the access stage cannot end the run there.
findings.fix: Keep the in-lab actions available until the debrief. For example, render a compact InLabChoices panel (the time since onset, atropine, the cough, stopping the infusion, external pacing, and the finish button when restored) whenever `sc.inLab && inLab && stage !== "debrief"`. Hide only 'Wait' and 'Femoral venous wire' once the stage has passed assess. Add a pacing.inlab.test or PacingLab.test case: in inlab-amiodarone-avb, record femoral-wire at t=12 and then stop-infusion at t=20, and check that the initial-management item scores 20.

findings.where: src/ui/bedside/PacingLab.tsx initialAction("external-pacing") (calls recordAction(a) before the branch that only sets pads)
findings.problem: Pressing the 'External pacing' button records the expected action, and scorePacing gives its share of the initial-management points. That happens even if transcutaneous pacing is never started or never captures, because the button only ticks the pads box. changeTcp already records the action when TCP is actually switched on, so the button double-counts and overstates the credit.
findings.fix: In initialAction, skip `recordAction(a)` for "external-pacing". Keep setPads(true) and the log line, and let changeTcp (t.on) record the action. Alternatively, have scorePacing award the external-pacing share only when `log.tcpUsed` is true. Add a test that pads without TCP earns no external-pacing share.

findings.problem: The header still says 'The deprecated stage aliases "pacing" and "pericardiocentesis" are never reported (DEPRECATED_LAB_PHASES)', but pacingTipContext now reports `phases: ["pacing"]` at every stage. That also cuts against the comment on DEPRECATED_LAB_PHASES in src/content/lab/tips.ts ('no lab should report them in new code'). Reporting the alias is needed to meet the acceptance criterion that tipsFor(ctx, 20) returns the bed-pace tips before tip-retarget-catchup runs. Side effect: the reachability report now counts bed-pace-overdrive-vt as satisfiable, although the lab hides it. The `"pacing" as string as LabPhase` cast removes the compiler's guard, so if the alias leaves the vocabulary first, this file will report an unknown phase without any warning.
findings.fix: Rewrite lines 18-19 to say that the pericardiocentesis tab never reports a deprecated alias, and that the pacing tab reports 'pacing' as a transitional alias until tip-retarget-catchup, as described below. Drop the double cast and type it as `readonly LabPhase[] = ["pacing"]`. The compiler then forces tip-retarget-catchup to remove the alias here when it leaves the vocabulary. Record in the report that the catchup must also delete PACING_ALIAS_PHASES and refinePacingTips.

findings.where: src/simulation/pacing.inlab.test.ts 'acceptance: output entered in volts at 3x threshold...' and the persistent adenosine acceptance
findings.problem: The volts acceptance test is close to tautological. At the default 1000 ohm, volts and mA are the same number. The output-margin criterion compares two mA values, so it does not depend on the units. In the 500 ohm loop, inLabCriteria still formats with the default impedance, so the test never checks the displayed values. Nothing exercises the path the lab actually uses: Knob in volts, then stepOutputIn, then outputFrom, then changeOutput, then capture-loss threshold detection. In the persistent adenosine test, supportedAt is set by hand (`tPace + 2`) instead of coming from rhythmSupported over the run. The exam-render test checks the tips panel only through aria-label="Technique". As a design note, at 1000 ohm the V/mA switch changes only the unit label, which weakens the 'read the units' teaching point.
findings.fix: Add a test that drives the real conversion. With units "V", start the dial at 3 V, step down with stepOutputIn(v, -1, "V") and outputFrom, and advance the rhythm at each step until capture is lost. Take the last captured value as the threshold, as changeOutput does, then set 3 times it with the volt dial and assert capture plus the output-margin criterion. Repeat in mA. In the adenosine acceptance, find supportedAt by stepping advanceRhythm in 0.25 s increments until rhythmSupported first returns true. In PacingLab.test.ts, assert that the exam render lacks the LabTipsPanel section's own aria-label/title.

rejected: Finding 1 (src/ui/lab/bedsideTips.test.ts:85 expects raises.procedures to be ['pericardiocentesis']): I checked it and it is correct, but I can't make the change. That file belongs to pericardiocentesis-tips-and-pci-handover and is not on this package's list. It still fails 1 of its 11 tests. The coordinator or the owning package should switch lines 73-85 to PERIC_RAISES, which is already exported from ./bedsideTips. The final assertion should become expect(raises.procedures).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(['pericardiocentesis','pacing','tcp'])).

Finding 5 (docs/realism/facts has no pacing entry): this is also correct but outside my list of files. The coordinator should create docs/realism/facts/pacing.md and list these as MODEL PARAMETER values: LEAD_IMPEDANCE_OHM 1000, TIGHT_SHEATH_TORQUE 0.35, IN_LAB_MODEL (waitS 30, coughEffectS 2, atropineOnsetS 20), timeLimitS 180/60/300, atropineAtrialFactor 1.2/1.2/1.1, transient resolvesAfterS 12, and the rhythm numbers of the three in-lab scenarios and their exam variants. fix.notes:
I applied five of the seven findings. The other two (1 and 5) need files outside this package and are listed under rejected for the coordinator. The package's own tests pass and the typecheck is clean. One test in another package's file still fails: bedsideTips.test.ts line 85 (finding 1).

Finding 2 (pacing dependence shown on live screens), in /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/ui/bedside/PacingLab.tsx:
- The test checklist now says "Pacing dependent: do not turn the rate down" only in guided practice.
- In exam, supervised and independent runs it shows one neutral sensing row instead. Its button, "Pacing dependent: sensing not tested", is offered whenever sensing has been neither tested nor skipped, so the learner makes the call.
- The "mV or lower" sensitivity advice now shows only in guided practice.
- Extra change: offering the button in every scenario would have let a learner earn the sensing points by skipping where sensing could be tested. To stop that, the lab notes when the button is pressed whether the patient really was pacing dependent at that moment. The log's sensingSkippedDependent is true only in that case, so a wrong skip earns no credit.
- TestChecklist and InLabChoices are now named exports so they can be rendered directly in tests.

Finding 3 (in-lab actions locked after the assess stage):
- After assess, a compact in-lab panel stays on screen in every stage until the debrief. It shows the time since onset, atropine, the cough, stopping the infusion, external pacing, and the finish button once conduction is back. Wait and the femoral wire are hidden.
- Tests: in pacing.inlab.test.ts, the femoral wire at t=12 then stopping the infusion at t=20 scores 20 for initial management. In PacingLab.test.ts, the compact amiodarone panel renders the stop-infusion button.

Finding 4 (the External pacing button earned credit by itself):
- Pressing the button now only puts the pads on; the action is recorded when transcutaneous pacing is switched on (changeTcp).
- The button is disabled while the pads are on.
- scorePacing (src/simulation/pacing.ts) counts external pacing only when log.tcpUsed is true (pacing that captured).
- Test: with tcpUsed false, the external-pacing share is not awarded.

Finding 6 (bedsideTips.ts header and the alias cast):
- The header now says the pericardiocentesis tab never reports a deprecated alias, and the pacing tab reports "pacing" until tip-retarget-catchup.
- PACING_ALIAS_PHASES is typed `readonly LabPhase[] = ["pacing"]` with no cast. Its comment says tip-retarget-catchup must delete PACING_ALIAS_PHASES and refinePacingTips.

Finding 7 (weak tests):
- New test in pacing.inlab.test.ts that drives the real dial in three settings: volts at 1000 ohm, mA, and volts at 500 ohm. It steps down from 3 with stepOutputIn and outputFrom, advancing the rhythm at each step. It takes the threshold the way changeOutput does and checks that every non-refractory spike above it captured. It then turns the same dial up to three times the threshold and checks capture, rhythmSupported and the output-margin criterion. One dial step short of the target fails.
- In the persistent adenosine test, supportedAt now comes from stepping 0.25 s until rhythmSupported first returns true.
- On the tips-panel check: aria-label="Technique" is already LabTipsPanel's own default title. I added a second check that the exam render lacks "Ask for a tip".

fix2.notes:
I applied four of the six findings and rejected two, both because their fixes sit in files outside this package. All package tests pass and the typecheck is clean.

1. V/mA switch changed only the unit label (major, applied). In src/simulation/pacing.ts I changed LEAD_IMPEDANCE_OHM from 1000 to 500. It is still labelled MODEL PARAMETER, and the comment now gives the reason. The two dials now read differently: 1.6 mA reads 0.8 V, and the default 5 mA reads 2.5 V.
   - Oxford's anchors still hold. The acceptable threshold (below 1 mA) reads below 0.5 V, which is inside 'ideally 1 V or less'. 3 V is within the volt dial, and the apex threshold of every in-lab scenario reads 1 V or less.
   - At 500 ohm the volt dial's lower limit came out at 0.05 V, which the 0.1 V steps cannot reach. outputLimits now rounds the volt limits onto the dial: 0.1 to 10 V. The milliamp limits are unchanged.
   - Tests in src/simulation/pacing.inlab.test.ts: I updated the impedance and "2.5 V" assertions and added a test that the two readings differ and the anchors hold.

2. Lower-cased zone label (minor, applied). inLabCriteria now writes 'Wire secured. Final position: RV apex.' using ZONE_LABEL unchanged. A new test checks it.

3. Coaching on unscreened moves in exam mode (minor, applied). In src/ui/bedside/PacingLab.tsx the live warning now appears only in guided practice. Every move made without fluoroscopy is counted in a blindMoves ref. Outside guided practice the debrief log reports the count ('N lead moves were made without screening...').

4. Patient still coughs after long standstill (minor, applied).
   - Engine: a new MODEL PARAMETER, IN_LAB_MODEL.unresponsiveAfterS = 20 s. The comment cites the module text: coughing can keep the patient conscious, and persistent standstill is treated as an unconscious patient. A new function, patientResponsive(rhythm, inLabState, t), compares the time since the last ventricular beat (or the onset) with that interval. A beat of any origin (escape, conducted, paced or external) restores it.
   - PacingLab: the 250 ms tick logs 'The patient no longer responds.' or 'The patient is responding again.' on each change. In guided adenosine runs it also logs Brilakis's brief-CPR advice. The cough button is disabled and marked '(no response)'. If initialAction('cough') is still called, it logs that the patient does not respond and records nothing.
   - Effect on the plan's acceptance test: the engine test 'waiting 30 s and a cough do not restore conduction' still passes. In the app, though, a learner who waits the full 30 s first can no longer cough. That matches the module text's point that waiting passively in an unconscious patient is wrong.
   - I added no CPR action; it would need its own design.
   - New tests: an engine test of responsiveness (lost after 20 s of standstill, regained with capture, never lost in the RCA scenario with an escape rhythm or outside an in-lab run) and a render test of the disabled '(no response)' cough button in src/ui/bedside/PacingLab.test.ts.
